CSV TOWN FLAG: the site is at Kiradu village in the Thar Desert, about 35 km from Barmer city - CSV town 'Barmer' is approximate; documented with the corrected town. A group of ruined 11th-12th century Hindu temples built by Paramara vassals of the Chalukyas (Solanki) in the Maru-Gurjara (Solanki-mode) style, famous for erotic and sensuous carving ('Khajuraho of Rajasthan'). Of the five surviving structures the Someshvara temple (Shiva) is the best preserved, though its shikhara has collapsed. Kiradu (Kiratakupa/Kiradkot) was a Paramara capital on Thar trade routes; an 1178 CE inscription records repairs to a temple damaged by the Turushkas. The ruins are ASI-restored and ASI-protected (per tourism sources; the ASI notification was not independently verified in this pass).
